newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MALAYSIA 3-MONTH KLIBOR FIXED AT 8.04 PCT.
newsitem.headline: MALAYSIA 3-MONTH KLIBOR FIXED AT 8.04 PCT.

text.p: Malaysia's benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) was fixed at 8.04 percent at 0300 GMT.
It was at 8.16 percent on Wednesday.
The one-month KLIBOR was fixed at 8.01 percent against 8.21 percent on Wednesday.
KLIBOR is fixed by taking an average of rates offered by various banks in the country.
Money market dealers said the drop in interbank rates was expected after a sharp fall in the overnight rate on Wednesday.
The overnight fell to 5.5 percent from 8.0 percent on Tuesday due to aggressive lending by foreign banks long on ringgit.
"Foreign banks are still lending on the one-week and one-month this morning," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
"Foreigners are long and with ringgit still weak, the only option is for them to lend out the money," he said.
One-week money was at 7.5 percent this morning, against 8.0 percent on Wednesday.
Dealers said interbank rates were expected to come off further due to maturity of Bank Negara bills worth one billion ringgit on Friday.
